titulo: Google myths that leave you without visits
hooks: Will a website put you first on Google?
Google doesn't find you by magic
Why your competitors show up and you don't
voz: If I have a website, I show up first. I wish. That takes clear copy, a fast site and time. Google only looks at keywords. It also checks speed and how you look on phones. You have to pay to show up. A Google Maps listing and a good site get you found without ads.

captions: Having a website is step one to showing up on Google. Then comes copy that says what you do and where, a site that loads fast, and a little patience.
Google looks at way more than keywords: whether your site loads fast, whether it looks good on a phone, and whether it answers what people are searching for.
A Google Maps listing is free and it's often the first thing someone sees when they search for your kind of business nearby. If you don't have one, start there.
fuente: Google Search Central: mobile-first indexing and page experience signals (Core Web Vitals); Google Business Profile is free.
